newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia farmers seek loans to grow coffee.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia farmers seek loans to grow coffee.

text.p: Farmers in Indonesia's key coffee growing region of Lampung are seeking loans to expand cultivation of the Arabica variety, the official Antara news agency reported on Monday.
The agency said the request was made to the government's plantation affairs official in Lampung, Tibrizi Asmarantaka, during a weekend meeting.
Antara said the farmers complained that Arabica seedlings were expensive compared to the widely planted Robusta variety.
"We need loans to expand cultivation of Arabica coffee," Antara quoted one farmer as saying.
Indonesia, the world's largest coffee producer after Brazil and Colombia, grows mostly the Robusta variety which fetches a lower price than Arabica, considered to be of better quality.
Asmarantaka said there were already several private firms that gave loans to farmers to plant Arabica.
He said Arabica coffee was expected to be planted on some 10,000 hectares by mid-1999 in the Lampung area, compared with the present 1,648 hectares.
"Developing Arabica cultivation does not mean we are replacing Robusta coffee. We are going to plant Arabica only in places which are suitable," he said.
